steps_h2: How to Make a Product File in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: You finish with a file you can post. Open the guide, make the file, then post it.

steps.d: Pick today's job: the phone photo, the white main image, the first video, the size, or the test.
Upload the photo or paste a product link, follow that guide, and read the credit cost before you start.
The download has no watermark, so your store and a paid ad can both use it.

faq.q: What seller job does each guide finish for me?
faq.a: Short how-tos for one seller job each. They cover a phone photo, a plain main image, a first video ad, the frame each app wants, and a fair test of versions.

faq.q: How do I turn a guide into a file I can post?
faq.a: Follow the steps, upload your product photo or paste the product page, and make the file on the tool that guide names. The guide is the plan. The tool makes the file.

faq.q: Why use a guide instead of hiring someone to film?
faq.a: A photo on the kitchen table is enough to start after you close. Hiring someone to film means waiting on their calendar. The guide uses the picture you can take yourself.
Someone packing orders who has never booked a studio. A marketer can use the same pages when a client needs a file this week.

faq.q: Can I make a file if I have never edited video?
faq.a: Yes. You need a phone photo, not a timeline. The first-ad guide stops at a file you can post. Setting up the ad account stays in that app.

faq.q: Which kinds of shops can follow these steps?
faq.a: The same photo steps and video steps work across shops. Rules differ by product type, so check the industry page for your shop before you upload.

faq.q: Can one phone photo of my product feed every guide?
faq.a: Yes, if it shows the whole item clearly. A still and a clip made from it are separate files, each with its own credit cost.

faq.q: Where can I post the file once I download it?
faq.a: Wherever the guide's shape fits. A tall file is the phone placement. A square sits in a feed. The [platform pages](page:video-hub) name the usual frames. Your own store can use the download too.

faq.q: How many credits do a photo and a clip cost?
faq.a: A product photo is 24 credits. A 6-second clip is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. You see the cost before it starts. If a job fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Can I run the file in ads and on my store?
faq.a: Yes. Use it in ads and on your store. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: Which guide gives me a video with a person and a voice?
faq.a: The first-ad guide does, when you want a person on screen. You can also keep the frame on the product and still have a spoken line. The photo guides stop at a still.

faq.q: Why follow a guide instead of a blank start?
faq.a: The guide names the one task, the file you should end with, and the checks to make before you spend credits on a second try.

reviews.h2: How Sellers Use a Guide, Then Make the File
reviews.lead: Four sellers match today's job, drop in the product they ship, and post one file.

items.d: They check a sharp phone photo of the sage canvas tote, then make the file that guide names. They skip shooting that tote a second time before the first file is even posted.
They photograph the bamboo lunch container on the kitchen table by the window they already have. They skip booking a studio for that container.

items.t: Make the Plate the Main Image
items.d: They set the ceramic plate fully inside a bright white backdrop and use that still as the main image. The guide tells them when the plate is ready to post.
They change one thing between two plain fabric pouches and keep the version they want to run. They skip filming a new pair for every idea.
